differences.what: the front's composition and proportions: 23 points read on both pictures fit one scale and one level camera square to the front at 3.8 px RMS (0.13 m), so the plate draws the same front the photograph shows, and the build laid to the photograph stands on the plate's lines: the ogee gable's outline and crest, the attic light, the paired light, the oriel, the ground window, the door under its three pinnacles, the small light and the stoop overlay the pen lines within a few pixels (T-3365)
the crest's top and the three basement lights drawn about 0.28 m higher than the build's (8 px), the largest residuals of the fit; the oriel's lights about 0.25 m taller at their head
the gable's south foot: the plate's coping runs on down past the paired light's hood to the party side at about the same place as the build's run-on, where the right-hand tree takes it
the gable's coping drawn as a heavy rolled band, broader than the build's, and the roof slope north of the gable read as the coping's own shading: a pen's weight, not a form

the gable's pendant drawn as a foliate finial over the hood where the build draws stepped blocks, and the oriel's frieze as large carved cartouches where the build lays rings (the photograph's record holds both within tolerance)

the basement's three lights drawn filled with scrolled ironwork where the photograph shows plain dark openings and the build glazed lights: the two pictures disagree, and the photograph is read as the better witness of a detail this small
the near tall stack: on the build's place and width, its cap drawn about 0.5 m lower than the render's where the photograph's camera puts the top within 0.1 m: two pictures disagree

the second north stack: the plate draws none over the gable's north slope, and from this camera the build's rear stack hides behind the near one as the plate has it (this is what fixed the eye's place; see the camera's solve)
the stack at the plate's left edge (x 165-185 px in the vignette): about 1.5 m or more north of the north wall through this camera, so 2005's, as the photograph's record reads its far stack
the north flank and the near stack's breast: the left-hand tree covers them

the paired light's group and the course under it fall to the south in the plate (its hood about 0.06, its course about 0.11) while this camera, fitted square to the front, renders them level: the photograph's camera, re-solved by T-3365, shows the fall is the view's, not the building's (a camera turned 22.4 degrees south of square; through it the course and hood are level at 9.2 and 11.3 m), and the plate, drawn from about the photograph's place, carries the same turn more gently. Two camera fits differ here, not the house: this camera is still the square fit, its scale taken in the photograph's former square metres, and a turned refit of it is owed

the oriel's top: the plate draws its carved frieze up nearly to the course, about 0.5-0.6 m over the build's oriel crown (8.45 m), where the photograph shows about 0.5 m of brick between the oriel's moulded top and the course (T-3365); the two pictures disagree, and the photograph is read as the better witness, as for the basement lights
the two leafy trees either side of the front: not this record's (the parkway's and the yard's trees)
colour: a pen drawing; the stacks' brick, the front's red-brown and the basement's brownstone are the photograph's record's and the register's to say
the walk, the parkway and the street before the house: the plate's ground, not this record's
